Why shops outgrow what they have

The job is not a deal, and it is not a construction project

A cabinet job has a shape no general tool models. It gets measured, priced off linear feet and sheet yield, approved with drawings, nested, cut, finished, and installed — and every one of those stages can send it backwards. Shops end up running the real work in a spreadsheet and using the CRM as a contact list.

Quotes live in spreadsheets

Priced by linear foot and material, rebuilt from scratch every time, and impossible to compare against what the job actually cost.

Approvals live in email

The signed-off drawing is in someone's inbox, and so is the change order that made it wrong.

Capacity lives in someone's head

Whether you can take the job depends on what is on the CNC in three weeks, and only one person knows.

How it works

Six stages, the ones your shop already uses

  1. 01

    Measure

    Log the site visit, photos and wall dimensions from your phone. The measure becomes the job.

  2. 02

    Quote

    Price from linear feet, material and finish. Paste or import a cut list and Aglet prices against it.

  3. 03

    Approve

    Send drawings for client sign-off. Approvals and change orders are recorded against the job, not the inbox.

  4. 04

    Cut

    Push the approved cut list to the floor. Sheet count and nesting yield tracked per job.

  5. 05

    Finish

    Track finish schedule and booth time — the stage that quietly sets your real lead time.

  6. 06

    Install

    Schedule the crew, close the punch list, and lock the job so quoted-versus-actual is final.

What's in it

Built around a cut list, not a contact record

Quote from a cut list

Import or paste a door schedule and price it by linear foot, species, finish and hardware. Save the build-up as a template for the next kitchen.

Shop-stage pipeline

Measure, Quoting, Approved, Cutting, Finishing, Install — with backwards moves tracked, because that is what actually happens.

Capacity by machine

See what is on the CNC and in the booth by week, so you can answer "can we take this?" without walking the floor.

Client approvals and change orders

Drawings out, sign-off back, every revision timestamped against the job. The change order is attached to the money it moved.

Sheet and material tracking

Sheets consumed, nesting yield and remnants per job — so material variance stops being a surprise at year end.

Margin per job

Quoted versus actual on material, labour and finish time. The report that tells you which kind of work to stop taking.

Questions

What shops ask first

Does this replace Mozaik or Cabinet Vision?

No. Those design and nest the work; Aglet runs the job around them. Aglet takes the cut list your CAD produces and handles quoting, approvals, scheduling and margin. Keep cutting the way you already do.

Can I bring my open jobs over?

Yes — import from CSV, including the half-finished ones. Most shops are running live inside an afternoon.

Is this accounting software?

No. Aglet tracks quoted versus actual per job and exports to QuickBooks. Your bookkeeper keeps their tools.

Do my installers need a login?

They get a mobile job view — drawings, measurements, punch list — without a full seat. Field users do not count against your user limit.

What if we do commercial casework too?

Same pipeline. Commercial jobs carry longer approval chains and submittal tracking, which is what the Mill tier adds.
